sources_considered.why: Primary year-end 2023 job-cut report that counts cuts attributed to AI.
Reputable report on the best-known 2023 case of AI replacing workers, which failed.
Company's own February 2024 claim that its AI support bot did the work of 700 agents with quality on par with humans.
Secondary coverage of the Klarna release. The primary release was used instead.

receipt.public_excerpt: Companies cited Artificial Intelligence for 4,247 cuts in 2023

evidence_items.explanation: Supports part 1. Only 4,247 announced US job cuts in 2023 were attributed to AI, about 0.6% of all announced cuts that year (see e2).
Total announced cuts. This is the base for the share in e1.

receipt.public_excerpt: An AI-powered chatbot that replaced employees at an eating disorder hotline has been shut down after it provided harmful advice

evidence_items.explanation: Supports part 2. The best-known 2023 case of a chatbot replacing staff ended with the bot pulled for giving harmful advice.

receipt.public_excerpt: It is on par with human agents in regard to customer satisfaction score

evidence_items.explanation: Contradicts part 2. Klarna, the most prominent replacement case at the time, said its AI did the work of 700 agents with customer satisfaction on par with humans. This is the company's own claim, not independently checked.

unresolved_gaps: Challenger counts only cuts where employers named AI as the reason, so it may miss quieter displacement. The hedge 'does not appear' fits this limit.
Klarna's quality figures are self-reported. No independent check of the results was found from within the period.
No systematic data on the outcomes of AI replacements in 2023 and early 2024 was found.
